note: Typical El Niño effects. Every El Niño is different, so these are tendencies, not guarantees.

regions.name: California
regions.impact: More and stronger storms and atmospheric rivers, flooding, coastal erosion, king tide flooding and landslides.
regions.prepare: Know your flood risk, get sandbags early, clear drains and plan for power outages.

regions.name: Pacific Northwest (U.S.)
regions.impact: A milder winter with less snowpack, which can mean water shortages and wildfire risk the next summer.
regions.prepare: Conserve water and watch for drought notices.

regions.name: Southern U.S. and Gulf Coast
regions.impact: More winter rain and flooding across the Southeast and Gulf Coast.
regions.prepare: Check flood zones and keep storm drains clear.

regions.name: Peru and Ecuador
regions.impact: Heavy coastal rain, river flooding and mudslides. Warmer ocean water hurts fishing.
regions.prepare: Make a family emergency plan and know where to evacuate.

regions.name: South Asia (Nepal, India, Bangladesh)
regions.impact: El Niño years often bring a weaker or delayed monsoon, which means drought, heat and lost crops for farming families.
regions.prepare: Save water, plan for heat, and ask local farm offices about drought-tolerant seed.

regions.name: Indonesia and Australia
regions.prepare: Prepare for wildfire smoke and water limits.

regions.name: Southern Africa
regions.prepare: Follow local drought and food-security programs.

regions.name: East Africa
regions.prepare: Know flood-safe routes and higher ground.

regions.name: Central America
regions.impact: Drought in the Dry Corridor, with crop losses.
regions.prepare: Plan water storage and watch crop advisories.
